perf.summary: Insertion sort is O(n^2); for the unbounded len contract this degrades badly. A specialized integer sort (e.g. LSD radix sort on 64-bit keys, or an introsort/heapsort hybrid) gives O(n) / O(n log n) worst case.
perf.currentCost: O(n^2) comparisons+moves in the worst/average case. For len in the thousands this is millions of ops; the inner while is a serial dependency chain (each ptr[j+1]=ptr[j] depends on the prior), so it cannot vectorize and stalls the pipeline.
perf.proposedChange: Provide a threshold-dispatched Run: keep insertion sort for small len (e.g. len <= 32 or 64), and for larger len run an LSD radix sort over the 8 bytes of the long (8 passes of 256-bucket counting sort, flipping the sign bit of the top byte to handle signed ordering). Radix needs one scratch buffer of len longs; reuse a caller-provided buffer to honor the no-managed-alloc constraint (Run(long* ptr, long* scratch, int len)).
perf.rationale: Radix sort is O(8n) = O(n) for 64-bit keys vs O(n^2). Counting passes are branchless and cache-friendly (sequential reads, histogram in stackalloc int[256]). Removes the long serial dependency chain of insertion sort. Keeping insertion for tiny len preserves its low constant-factor advantage where radix's 8 passes lose.
perf.risk: Signed ordering: must XOR the most-significant byte with 0x80 (flip sign bit) so two's-complement negatives sort before positives; do it only on the top-byte pass and reverse on read, or pre/post transform. Stability differs from insertion sort but sort is not documented as stable for scalars. Requires an API change to take scratch (or stackalloc only when len is small) — flag as additive overload, not a silent break.
